body:
Triage (first-touch, triage seat, session `session_01HXzdkKx5WjwwCTT3c7U5kB`): filed correctly in objectui (console-owned top bar); type Feature — rendering a current-organization indicator adds UI surface, so this is a maintainer call, not a dispatchable defect. `needs-user-decision`. Real measured pull attached (downstream acceptance run, case S20-001 with archived screenshots).

<!-- os-decision-facets -->
- platform long-term coherence: under `isolated` tenancy "which org am I in" is load-bearing context, and the console owns the top bar — a read-only indicator for single-membership users completes the multi-org surface consistently (switcher stays the multi-membership affordance) rather than adding a special case; app projects have no metadata hook to self-serve this.
- measured business pull: measured, not speculative — a downstream project's multi-tenant acceptance run failed on it (steedos-labs/os-project-titanwind-ehr#1577 case S20-001); any single-membership business user on an isolated deployment is affected today.
- AI-agent error-resistance: neutral-to-positive — a console-owned indicator prevents each downstream app from hacking its own org display (the workaround pressure is already visible in the filing).
- startup scope discipline: small bounded addition (render an already-session-known datum read-only); still a permanent console surface, and Feature-class stays a human call.

Recommendation: **A** — when the org context is active and the user has exactly one membership, render the current organization name read-only in the top bar; switcher continues to render only for multi-membership. Options: A (read-only indicator) / B (always render switcher, single-entry disabled) / C (decline; document that single-membership users see no org name).
Confidence gap: not verified whether the top bar already receives the active-org datum for single-membership sessions (may need a fetch, which changes the cost), nor whether other tenancy postures expect the bar to stay org-silent.

Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — the render is small; the precondition below is where the judgement is.
Clause-②: no — this renders a datum the session already carries (or fetches one, see the precondition). No schema accept/reject boundary moves and no authoring surface widens. The card's **type is `Feature`**, which is why it went to the maintainer first; it has been ruled, so it is now ordinary dispatchable work.
Serial constraints cleared: nothing open touches the console top bar. **PR5327 (#5309, `app-shell/.../metadata-admin/inspectors/**`) merged this round** — if your surface lands in `packages/app-shell`, it is a different subtree and the file is free; still rebase and re-read.

## Zone 1 — RULED. Option A. Do not re-open the ballot.

Maintainer, 2026-08-19, verbatim 「全部接受」, recorded on this card:

> ## Ruling: Option A — read-only current-organization indicator for single-membership users
> - The console top bar renders the current organization name **read-only** when org context is active and the user has **exactly one** membership; the workspace switcher itself **stays hidden** when there is nothing to switch to. Option B (switcher with one disabled entry) and C (decline + document) are rejected.
> - Implementation precondition from the confidence gap: **first verify whether the top bar already receives the active-org datum for single-membership sessions — if a new fetch is needed, size it in the PR rather than assuming.**

⛔ **Do not implement B by accident.** "Render the switcher but disable it" is the rejected option, and it is the shape you will drift into if you start from the existing switcher component and relax its render condition. The switcher's visibility rule is unchanged; what you are adding is a separate read-only indicator for the case the switcher declines to render.

## Zone 2 — the precondition is a deliverable, not a preamble

**Measure, before you write the component, whether the top bar already has the active organization's name for a single-membership session.** Three outcomes, and they have very different costs:

1. **Already present** (the session/context already carries it) — render it; this is a small PR.
2. **Present but only populated on the multi-membership path** — the datum exists and something skips fetching or storing it for single-membership users. Say exactly where, then fix that rather than adding a second source.
3. **Genuinely absent** — a new fetch is needed. **Size it in the PR body** — what call, on what render, cached how. ⛔ Do not add an unconditional per-page-load request without saying so plainly.

Report which of the three you measured, with the file and line. **A zero is not a reading until you counter-probe it** with a datum you know the bar does receive.

## The other half of the confidence gap — check it, do not assume it

The triage note also flags: *"nor whether other tenancy postures expect the bar to stay org-silent."* So: **what does a single-org / non-isolated / degraded deployment render after your change?** The ruling scopes the indicator to "when org context is active" — find what makes that predicate true in this codebase and gate on it. A single-tenant deployment growing an organization name in its top bar would be a visible regression for every existing user, and it is the most likely way this change goes wrong.

## Tests

- Org context active + **exactly one** membership ⇒ the organization name is rendered, read-only, and **no switcher control** is present.
- Org context active + **multiple** memberships ⇒ unchanged: switcher renders, current org visible through it. ⛔ Do not regress this path.
- **Org context inactive / single-tenant posture ⇒ nothing new renders.** This is the regression guard; write it even though it feels obvious.
- The indicator is genuinely read-only — no click target, no menu.

Reverse-verify: restore the component, keep the tests, **predict which go red before running**, report predicted vs observed. State per leg whether a build artifact sits between the edit and the thing under test (if your surface is in `packages/app-shell` and the test runs from `apps/console`, one does).

## Gates

Derive from your diff (`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is **objectstack-only**). Run vitest **from the repo root** — note the reason, because the guard's own header states it wrongly: it is not that a package-scoped run is refused (17 packages own a standalone `vitest.config.ts` and are not refused), it is that a package-scoped run uses **a different config than CI does**, so its green is not CI's green. Changeset: run `check-changeset-presence.mjs` and follow its verdict — `apps/console` is not a released package, `packages/app-shell` is. `patch` or `minor`; ⛔ **never `major`** (maintainer, 2026-08-19: 「objectui ui 的 major 是要跟着 objectstack 走的,不可以自己发 major」).

⛔ Do not background a long check and end your turn. ⛔ No exhaustive paginated API sweeps.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first body line `Fixes #5287`. Push the branch early. Return the JSON report and post it as a comment whose first line is the literal `<!-- os-dev-report -->` marker.

**One note on provenance**: this card was filed by a human from a downstream project's acceptance run (case S20-001), not by a sweep. The failing scenario is real and someone is waiting on it — if you find the fix is larger than the ruling assumed, say so early rather than shipping something narrower than what was ruled.
